about: Cases for the Script editor's house style, written from napkin-radio's own constants and comments (lib/radio/parse.ts tag table, lib/radio/quality.ts, lib/ai/house-style.ts at e1317fd). Both readers of house-style.json run this file: the page's JavaScript (app/tests/scriptEditor.test.ts) and, with the rewrite handlers, the middleware's Python. A case with a `differs` note changes napkin-radio's behaviour on purpose.

parse.name: the tag table's three voices, two cues, with ':' and '-' separators
parse.text:
FVO:  Have you tried the new brunch?
MVO - Best flat white in town.
SFX:  door swings open, cafe ambience
MUSIC: warm acoustic bed, low
VO:   Napkin Coffee. Weekends, sorted.

expect.text: Have you tried the new brunch?

parse.name: dotted acronyms and the '.' and ')' separators
parse.text:
F.V.O. - hello
M.V.O: yes
V.O) plain
S.F.X: rain

parse.name: aliases: FEMALE, MALE VO, ANNCR, NARRATOR, SOUND FX, MX, BED, JINGLE
parse.text:
FEMALE: a
MALE VO: b
ANNCR: c
NARRATOR: d
SOUND FX: e
MX: f
BED: g
JINGLE: h

parse.name: a counter digit on a tag is dropped
the legacy A and B speakers cast as FVO and MVO
parse.text:
A: hi
B: yo
Speaker A: again

parse.name: an untagged line carries on the voice line before it
copy before any tag is a neutral voice line
a colon that is not a known tag stays copy
an untagged line never folds into a cue
a bare cue tag keeps an empty line
parse.differs: napkin-radio fills 'Sound effect' or 'Music' here; the editor keeps the line empty so the writer sees it is empty.

parse.name: a TITLE line is not special
parse.differs: napkin-radio reads a leading TITLE: as the script's title; the editor's title is the document's.

read.name: a 78-word read is 30 seconds at 2.6 words a second
